Mina / Marissa — quick legal read. High-level: we should offer both routes but be explicit about the evidence expectations and timeline. Points below: 

- UK IDTA: we can execute the UK Addendum (dual-execution) for customers that require it, but recommend adding a 30-day evidence handoff SLA in the DPA (we should not accept 10 days unless escalated).
- SCCs + TIA: acceptable as an alternative when customers want shorter lead time; TIAs need to be scoped and limited to the datasets that actually travel (proposal: "clinical PII only" as Mina suggested).
- Subprocessor notifications: our standard is 30 days; if Medico insists on 10 we should push for 30 with an option to notify sooner for critical infra changes and provide interim mitigations (onshore cache + logging).
- Onshore cache & residency: ops (Jonas) — can you confirm whether we can pin the cache to a UK region for this workload and document the KV cache retention/eviction so it qualifies as a safeguard in the TIA?

I'll mark the attached DPA with two inline redlines: 1) explicit UK Addendum acceptance clause, and 2) a conditional TIA appendix template the customer can sign to limit routing. I attach the redlined PDF and a suggested TIA evidence map (spreadsheet).

-Kim
